plancap

plancap estimates the floorspace and dwellings that planning rules enable on each land parcel, for any jurisdiction, and summarises and plots the result.

Planning rules (height limits, setbacks, recession or daylight planes, site coverage, landscaping, floor area ratios, density controls, overlays and precincts) are entered as a rulebook: a validated set of rules with a citation for every value. You can write it as a YAML file, as a spreadsheet, or in R. Capacity is built site by site as a stack of storey footprints clipped by every rule that applies. The results can then be summarised by zone, height, location or the rule that binds.

Status: early development. The rulebook (rules, validation, YAML / JSON / Excel input) and example data are in place; site preparation, the engine, summaries and plots are being built in stages. See the development plan.

A rulebook 

library(plancap)

rb <- rulebook("Exampleton District Plan") |>
  add_zone(zone("MDR", "Medium Density Residential",
    height = height_limit(12, roof_allowance = 1, storeys = 3, source = "MDR-S1"),
    setbacks = list(
      yard(2.5, "road", source = "MDR-S3"),
      yard(1, c("side", "rear"), source = "MDR-S3"),
      plane(60, start_height = 4, boundaries = c("side", "rear"), source = "MDR-S2")
    ),
    coverage = ratio(0.5, source = "MDR-S4"),
    landscaping = ratio(0.2, source = "MDR-S5")))

validate_rulebook(rb)
rule_table(rb)
write_rulebook(rb, "exampleton.yaml")   # or .json, or .xlsx for a spreadsheet

Rulebooks for Exampleton and, as worked examples, Auckland, Christchurch and Wellington ship with the package: rulebook_example("wellington").

Scope

plancap estimates plan-enabled, gross, blank-slate capacity: what the rules would allow on each site if no buildings existed. It does not estimate feasible, infrastructure-ready or likely development.

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("faceteconomics/plancap")

Example data

exampleton() loads Exampleton, a synthetic town of about 1,500 parcels built so that every rule type has something to act on. It has corner, rear and through lots, a split-zoned block, height areas, a precinct, a river with a flood plain, protected trees, existing buildings and a ground surface. It is placed in the open sea so it cannot be mistaken for a real place.

library(plancap)
town <- exampleton()
names(town)
#>  [1] "parcels"          "road_centrelines" "zoning"           "height_areas"
#>  [5] "flood_hazard"     "heritage"         "precincts"        "water"
#>  [9] "transit"          "trees"            "buildings"
